batch_review: The batch contains 32 unique eligible records across 31 structures. The two selections on the same structure complete a matched ratio-by-preparation comparison. batch_review: Verified 32 distinct eligible IDs across 31 structures and their exact PE/EA anchors. The only two selections for one structure complete a matched load-by-ratio comparison using two existing measurements. Other load checks reuse measured counterparts. Isomer comparisons are marked as analogies, and comparisons that also change nominal sample volume are not called ratio-only contrasts. batch_strategy: Use matched solvent-ratio changes to learn how V1 and V2 respond within a structure, and first measurements on related unmeasured structures to test whether those responses transfer. Emphasize weak eluents where predictions diverge, while retaining stronger-eluent measurements for polar compounds and targeted loading contrasts where measured V1 and V2 behave differently.

batch_review: Checked 32 distinct current candidates across 32 structures. Comparisons that also change preparation, flow or load are not treated as ratio-only contrasts. No selection relies on a quantile width alone.
batch_strategy: Select rows that distinguish competing predictions for V1 and V2: fill gaps between measured solvent ratios, test extrapolation on related structures, and vary sample volume where a new label can resolve a consequential disagreement. Give priority to comparisons that inform several remaining rows.

hypothesis_updates.claim: For 4-nitrobenzophenone prepared with 1000 µL DCM at 50/1 PE/EA, the 150 µL sample will have a later V2 than the 50 µL sample, with a larger difference in V2 than the absolute difference in V1.
hypothesis_updates.relevance_to_model_learning: The middle load can distinguish gradual broadening from a response concentrated at one end of the load range. The sign and size of the effect should not be imposed on other structures.
hypothesis_updates.revision_reason: The matched 50/1 pair meets both criteria: 150 minus 50 µL gives +21.43 mL for V2 and -16.83 mL for V1. The interval widened by 38.26 mL. Unlike the 20/1 pair, the onset difference is substantial.
hypothesis_updates.unresolved_question: Does the 100 µL interval width fall between the two measured widths? The endpoint pair alone does not establish the shape or reproducibility of the load response.

feedback_interpretation: Acquisition-time errors had opposite signs even at 50/1: V2 was underestimated by 57.29 mL for the unsaturated aldehyde and overestimated by 45.08 mL for ortho-methoxyacetophenone. For methoxyethyl acetoacetate at 5/1, V1 was underestimated by only 3.47 mL while V2 was underestimated by 46.60 mL. These results favor separate tests of onset and interval width, not a global ratio correction. The nitrobenzophenone load contrast was supported; the earlier dimethoxybenzaldehyde preparation claim remains rejected.
